hook: Lightning's negative leaders advance as thin conducting filaments, not streamers as long assumed.
summary: LOFAR radio measurements of high-altitude negative leaders show the fan at the tip is made of thin filaments about 1 m in radius that grow smoothly over hundreds of meters and radiate steadily in VHF. This conflicts with the common picture of streamers at the tip. The conclusion is inferred from radio imaging of a limited set of events, not direct optical views of the filaments.
title: Filamentary dynamics in fan-like structures in high-altitude lightning discharges
